vulnerable.headline: reentrancy-eth - High impact, Medium confidence
vulnerable.detail: Reentrancy in VulnerableVault.withdraw() (VulnerableVault.sol#14-28): External calls: - (ok,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (VulnerableVault.sol#20) State variables written after the call(s): - balances[msg.sender] = 0 (VulnerableVault.sol#23) VulnerableVault.balances (VulnerableVault.sol#6) can be used in cross function reentrancies: - VulnerableVault.balances (VulnerableVault.sol#6) - VulnerableVault.deposit() (VulnerableVault.sol#9-12) - VulnerableVault.withdraw() (VulnerableVault.sol#14-28)

vulnerable.headline: SWC-107 State access after external call - Medium severity, line 23
vulnerable.detail: Write to persistent state following external call The contract account state is accessed after an external call to a user defined address. To prevent reentrancy issues, consider accessing the state only before the call, especially if the callee is untrusted. Alternatively, a reentrancy lock can be used to prevent untrusted callees from re-entering the contract in an intermediate state.

safe.headline: No state write after the external call
safe.detail: Explored 3 transactions to the configured depth and 300s timeout. 3 issue(s) of other kinds, 2 of them SWC-107 pattern warnings with no state write after the call.

safe.headline: CHC: assertion violation check is safe
safe.detail: The solvency assertion holds in every reachable state, for unbounded transaction sequences, including re-entrant callbacks from unknown external code.
